Write accepted study data (low level)

Source: R/data_management.R
add_study_data.Rd

Validates the metadata and data points against the extraction form and writes data/<study_id>/ (study.yml, metadata.yml, data.csv, provenance.csv and datapackage.json; see SPEC.md section 8). All validation problems are reported at once.

Usage

add_study_data(
  path = ".",
  study_id,
  metadata,
  data,
  reports = NULL,
  provenance = list(channel = "manual_edit"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  validate = TRUE
)

Arguments

path

Project root.

study_id

Study id (see check_study_id()), e.g. "hansen2019".

metadata

Named list matching the metadata part of the form. Arrays of objects may be given as data frames.

data

Data frame (or list of objects) matching data_points. May have zero rows.

reports

Reports (publications) of the study: a list of lists with doi, pmid and role (primary or secondary). Defaults to the existing reports, else metadata$doi/metadata$pmid.

provenance

Where the values came from: either a list of defaults (extraction_id, person, channel, tool, model, source_sha256, timestamp) applied to every data point, or a data frame with a measurement_id column (and _metadata for the metadata). When overwriting, the provenance of data points whose values did not change is kept.

overwrite

Replace an existing study? Defaults to FALSE.

validate

Validate before writing? Defaults to TRUE.

Value

The study folder, invisibly.

Details

This bypasses the submission workflow. Input channels should use submit_study() and accept_submission(), which call this function and record where each value came from.
